0.long_answer: Grover’s disease, also known as transient acantholytic dermatosis, was first reported by an American dermatopathologist in 1975. Histologically, it is notable for the loss of intercellular connections (acantholysis), a feature also seen in pemphigus vulgaris but absent in bullous pemphigoid, where the separation occurs at the dermoepidermal junction. Grover’s disease typically presents with pruritic, papulovesicular eruptions and, although its course can be transient, it highlights a unique pattern of intraepidermal acantholytic changes that differentiate it from other autoimmune bullous disorders.
